div.p: This minimal example demonstrates the laboratory report content discussed for CLIA and CAP using core FHIR 6.0.0 elements and four OO-owned resource profiles, with no extensions. A single potassium Observation carries the result; the supporting resources supply its clinical and reporting context. All people, laboratories, identifiers, and clinical values are illustrative.

The example declares conformance to Laboratory Report Content, Laboratory Result Content, Laboratory Specimen Content, and Laboratory Order Content. The result profile requires an actual value[x] and prohibits dataAbsentReason, including on any components. A valueless organizer or a result containing only a data absent reason cannot conform.

Each profiled resource has its own business identifier and assigning namespace. The specimen type is coded, and its availability and receipt time are included. These additions support identification and reconciliation of report content. The profiles also support correction context and additional specimen and result details informed by HL7 laboratory reporting guidance; this final-result example does not demonstrate the full LRI interface or correction workflow.

The Bundle is a collection, with all resource references resolving within it. It illustrates report content rather than a document, message, transaction, or delivery workflow. DiagnosticReport.performer identifies the referring laboratory responsible for issuing the report; Observation.performer identifies the separately registered referral laboratory that actually performed the test. In this scenario, the referral laboratory returns the result to the referring laboratory, which releases the report to the ordering clinician.

tr.td: 1. Testing laboratory name and address, including referral laboratory

Observation.performer resolves to Organization.name and Organization.contact.address. Both the referring and referral laboratories are included, each with a distinct fictional CLIA identifier in Organization.identifier.
Observation.subject and DiagnosticReport.subject resolve to Patient.name and Patient.identifier.
Observation.basedOn and DiagnosticReport.basedOn resolve to ServiceRequest; ServiceRequest.requester resolves to Practitioner.name.
Specimen.collection.collectedDateTime, including the time zone offset.
DiagnosticReport.issued records report release. Observation.issued records the earlier availability of the individual result.
Observation.specimen and DiagnosticReport.specimen resolve to Specimen.type (serum).
Observation.code and Observation.valueQuantity, with UCUM units.
Observation.referenceRange.low and high, with matching UCUM units. The interval is illustrative and must be appropriate to the performing laboratory's method and patient population in actual use.
Specimen.condition and Specimen.note describe slight hemolysis; Observation.note carries its potential effect on the potassium result.

div.p: The DiagnosticReport narrative also assembles these details into a readable report. A receiving system must preserve access to the linked content when presenting results to the clinician, including the testing laboratory's name and address and the specimen limitation. This content example does not establish regulatory or accreditation compliance: authorized release, referral result delivery, audit trails, critical-result notification, corrections, and retention require implementation workflows beyond this Bundle.
Background: 42 CFR 493.1291, Standard: Test report, and the FHIR DiagnosticReport resource. The numbered mapping follows the ten report-content requirements supplied for this example.
